workload: North America's Natural Earth land ring (19825 vertices) scan-filled into a 120 by 36 cell radar window over eastern Massachusetts.
notes: Each land ring is tested against every dot-row in its y-span. A regional radar window still receives the whole continent ring, so this call spends about 134 ms in Python on edges that mostly miss the screen. An active-edge walk in this function yields the same (y, xa, xb) runs and skips the edges that do not cross the current row.

workload: Hillshade of a 160 by 96 coastal elevation grid, the sub-pixels of a 160 by 48 cell terrain map, with the vendored climate families sampled inside the call.
notes: Every land sub-pixel computes slope and aspect with atan, hypot and atan2, then four more sines and cosines, for one Lambertian shade. That shade is the dot product of the exaggerated gradient and the sun, so the inverse trig can leave the loop without moving a channel. It is most of the cost of shading a new terrain view.

workload: Paeth unfilter of every scanline of one 256 by 256 RGB tile, a smooth height field in the shape of a terrarium map tile.
notes: Terrarium tiles are Paeth rows, and this walk is most of decoding one: a Python list per channel and a branch on every byte. Writing the reconstructed byte straight into the output buffer keeps the same scanlines and drops those lists. A map frame decodes several tiles of this size.

workload: decode_rgba of the vendored 3600 by 1800 climate.png, 8-bit grayscale with no scanline filter.
notes: The climate grid decodes to 26 MB of RGBA and peaks near 58 MB, because the inflated scanlines, the gray reconstruction, and a solid alpha plane are all live beside the output. Releasing each before the next is allocated stays inside this function and leaves the pixels unchanged.
